William Shakespeare

Childhood in Stratford

we Shakespeare was born in Stratford-upon-Avon, England,
in 1564, the sixth year of the reign of Queen Elizabeth I. He was
whristened on April 26 of that year, but the exact date of his birth
| is unknown. He was the third child and oldest son of John Shakespeare
and Mary Arden. Two sisters, Joan and Margaret, died before he was
born. The other children were Gilbert, a second Joan, Anne, Richard,
and Edmund. Shakespeare’s father was a prosperous gammer’and glove-
maker. He had also been the mayor
of the town for a while. However,
towards the end of his life John
Shakespeare lost most of his money.
and when he died in 1601 he left
William only a little real estate. Not
much is known about Shakespeare's
mother, Mary Arden, except that she
came from a wealthier family than

her husband.

= is in Warwickshire, the heart of England. In
Shakespeare's day it was well farmed and surrounded by many woods.
The town itself was prosperous and progressive. Young William went to

the local grammar school, where his lessons were probably mainly in Latin.
The education he received there was probably good; all four schoolmasters
at the school during Shakespeare’s time were graduates of Oxford University.
Nothing definite is known about his childhood, but from the content of his
plays, it seems he learned early in his life about the woods and fields,

the birds, insects, and small animals that lived there, and about the country
people he later portrayed: in his plays. He also seems to have gpiekedeup

an amazing stoek of facts about hunting, daawking; fishing, dances, music,
and other arts and sports and to have studied alchemy, astrology, folklore,
medicine, and law. As good writers do, he collected information both from
the books he read and from daily observation of the world around him.

Marriage and Life in London

n 1582, when he was 18, he married Anne Hathaway, a Stratford girl.
Anne was seven or eight years older than him. Their first daughter,
Susanna, was born in 1583, and in 1585 twins, a boy and a girl,
Hamnet and Judith, were born. What Shakespeare did between 1583
and 1592 is not known. Various stories are told. He may have taught
school, or worked in a lawyer's office, served on a rich man’s estate,
or travelled with a company of actors.
One famous story says that about 1584 he and some friends were caught
poaching and were forced to leave town! Or it could be that he was
already in London in 1588, working in the theatre as a page.
By 1592, however, we know that Shakespeare was definitely in London
and vy

already recognised as a talented actor and playwright.
He was then 28 years old.

Be 1592 and 1594, the Plague gaged in London and the theatres
were closed most of the time. During these years Shakespeare turned
to other types of writing and wrote his earliest sonnets and two long
narrative poems, Venus and Adonis and The Rape of Lucrece. The works
were well received and helped to establish him as a poet. -

Actor and Playwright

es 1598 Shakespeare worked in two theatres in a district

of London called Shoreditch, The Theatre and The Curtain.
He then moved across the River Thames to settle in a district called
Bankside near the new Globe Theatre. He was associated with this
theatre for the rest of his working life, eventually ewning*shares

in it, which garmed him a lot of money. He was later able to buy
properties in his home town of Stratford and acquired a jseatofearms
and the title of “Gentleman”. This was very important to him, for
in his day actors were classed legally with criminals and vagrants!

ueen Elizabeth I died in 1603 and her nephew, James I,

followed her to the ghrone. Shakespeare’s theatrical company was
taken under the king’s patronage and became known as the King’s
Company (previously it was the Earl of Derby's Company and later the
Lord Chamberlain’s). Shakespeare and the other actors were made
officers of the royal house and their company became
the most successful of its time.

lays by Shakespeare were also performed at the royal court and in

the castles of the nobles. After 1603 Shakespeare probably didn’t act
much himself, preferring to concentrate on writing plays. Although he
was considered a good actor (his favourite roles seem to have been old
Adam in As You Like It and the Ghost in Hamlet), it was as a
playwright that he achieved most success and fame.

good, and returned to Stratford and his family. In 1613 the Globe
Theatre burned down and he lost a lot of money, but still seemed to
have been quite wealthy as he was able to share in the financing
of The New Globe some months later. On April 23, 1616, Shakespeare
died at the age of 52. He was jburiedin the Church of the Holy Trinity
in Stratford. Today the house where he lived in Stratford is a museum
and The Globe Theatre, which he worked so hard to make successful,
has recently been rebuilt in London as a permanent venue for his works
and a memorial to Britain’s most famous writer.
